authoritative_for: Conversations owns its short-lived local App Server adapter, filters, typed normalized user-and-assistant corpus, stable references, completed-turn activity projection, completeness failures, and installation behavior published by this provider.
Each invocation owns and terminates only its private App Server process group and emits no retained Conversations database or index.
not_authoritative_for: Codex App Server owns task discovery, persisted metadata, pagination, storage compatibility, source records, and availability.
Conversations does not own task mutation, machine-wide task liveness, transcript interpretation, Codex authentication, or raw Codex storage.

covers: All supported public Conversations CLI and embedded-library outcomes for history exploration, exact task-summary reads, completed-turn activity, refresh, and development in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, private implementation helpers, unsupported App Server records, task mutation, raw storage access, model interpretation, and App Server's own behavior are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Conversations accesses local Codex task state only through the documented App Server JSON-RPC interface and never opens Codex JSONL or SQLite storage.
Ordinary reads request state-database-only metadata; refresh is the sole public operation that permits App Server metadata repair.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Task titles, working directories, stable references, activity counts, and normalized user and assistant text can be private and are written only to caller-selected process output.
Conversations retains no corpus, index, daemon state, or credentials; redirected output and inherited App Server diagnostics become the caller's retention responsibility.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release and entry contract versions are distinct from the selected Codex CLI and App Server protocol version.
Protocol or public-schema changes require compatible typed behavior, synthetic fixture proof, and documented fallback or explicit failure before an older contract is retired.
operational_limits: Every operation is bounded to one short-lived App Server launch; full-text search and export are proportional to selected histories and no persistent index or network service is offered.
No App Server availability, wall-clock latency, corpus-size, machine-wide liveness, or perpetual compatibility service-level objective is promised across this provider.
